hook: A dancer in a studio stretches, twists and curls at high, middle and low levels, then travels straight, curved and zigzag pathways that paint a ribbon on the floor. The class copies, guesses hidden pathways by drawing them in the air, and draws new pathways for the dancer.
outcome: Move at high, middle and low levels and travel in straight, curved and zigzag pathways, and read a pathway and its level from a floor map
sources: National Core Arts Standards, Dance (2014), grade K to 2 performance standards for DA:Cr1.1 and DA:Pr4.1 (levels; straight, curved and zigzag pathways; locomotor and nonlocomotor movement): https://www.nationalartsstandards.org/

Levels, pathways, personal space, locomotor and nonlocomotor movement as dance concepts: Anne Green Gilbert, Creative Dance for All Ages, 2nd ed. (Human Kinetics, 2015); Perpich Center for Arts Education, "The Elements of Dance" (Body, Action, Space, Time, Energy)
Walk, skip, gallop and slide as K-2 locomotor skills: SHAPE America, National Standards and Grade-Level Outcomes for K-12 Physical Education (2014), S1.E1: https://www.shapeamerica.org/standards/pe/
The six energy qualities in the dance engine (smooth, sharp, swing, suspend, collapse, shake): Perpich Center, "The Elements of Dance", Energy section
The studio, the dancer, the ribbons and the icons are drawn in code; the tune and sounds are generated in the browser
